subject: Re: Request for operational evidence: KMS gating, subprocessor map, and no-adaptive-training commitment
messages:
From: Lina Ortega <lina.ortega@medbyte.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Cho <aaron.cho@medbyte.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Request for ops evidence for procurement review

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the MedByte team liked Redwood's latency profile and the routing options. Procurement is running a final compliance pass. They have a short set of asks we need to include in our DPA/addendum:

1) Evidence that tenant keys can be segregated (KMS gating diagram or architecture sketch).
2) Current subprocessor inventory and which subprocessors have access to decrypted tenant data.
3) Confirmation of a "no-adaptive-training" or "no-model-updates-from-customer-data" commitment for our account, and operational proof of how that is enforced.

Can you send the diagrams and a short ops note we can attach to the DPA? If you prefer, Aaron and I can sign an NDA to receive any detailed ops docs.

Appreciate a reply by EOD Monday — procurement is on a fast track.

Best,
Lina Ortega
Head of Procurement, MedByte Health

Hi Lina — thanks and glad the demo went well.

We can provide the items you listed. High level:
- I attached a KMS segregation diagram (redacted) and an inventory export of subprocessors. The diagram highlights customer-specific KMS keys, HSM integration, and the onshore key escrow lanes.
- For the no-adaptive-training commitment, Redwood offers an operational guarantee for enterprise customers: we can opt your account into a "non-adaptive" mode where customer interactions are excluded from model improvement pipelines. That mode includes access controls, audit logging, and a verification report we run monthly.

I'm copying David (Privacy) and Jonas (Platform) to propose two deliverables: a one-page ops note describing enforcement and a short checklist that procurement can append to the DPA.

If MedByte needs deeper artifacts we can share them under an NDA or an evidence-sharing addendum.

Kimberly Park

Kimberly — quick notes for the ops artifacts.

1) KMS gating: the attached diagram is redacted to remove provider-internal network addresses. Jonas and I can produce an expanded version for MedByte under an evidence-sharing addendum (we'll need the recipient contact and an SOC/NDA clause).

2) Subprocessor inventory: the CSV includes subprocessors and functional roles; highlight rows where subprocessor processes decrypted content. We'll mark those for the procurement team.

3) No-adaptive-training enforcement: proposed operational proof bundle:
   - A short checklist (no-adapt-ops-checklist.docx) describing: request routing flags, exclusion from streaming-learning hooks, KV cache purge schedule, and monthly attestation logs.
   - A sample monthly attestation report (redacted) showing a per-account audit that verifies "no adaptive training" for the prior 30 days.

Marissa — can you prepare the checklist and a short narrative (<= 2 pages) describing roles who run the attestation and how log retention works? Also include the expected timeline to generate the expanded KMS diagram under addendum.

Thanks — I recommend we keep the MedByte team in the loop while we draft the addendum language.

-David
David Kim
Senior Privacy Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request for ops evidence for procurement review

Attached: no-adapt-ops-checklist.docx (draft).

Draft summary for procurement (to drop into DPA addendum):
- Commitment: MedByte's tenant(s) will be enrolled in Redwood's Non-Adaptive mode; customer-generated interaction data will be tagged and excluded from model improvement pipelines at ingestion and at any downstream telemetry collection points.
- Enforcement: exclusion flagging occurs at API ingress and is enforced by the routing layer; logs are produced and stored in the account's audit bucket for 90 days by default (longer retention available per contract).
- Verification: monthly attestation prepared by Platform Compliance (sample redacted report available). Attestation includes a checksum of exclusion flags, recent routing decisions, and a KV cache purge confirmation.
- KMS: keys for MedByte are customer-managed within supported KMS providers; Redwood maintains an onshore escrow path and a documented handoff procedure for recovery.

Timeline: 48 business hours to provide the expanded KMS diagram and a redacted sample attestation (we will provide under an evidence-sharing addendum).

Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we loop legal:

- Will the attestation call out that model checkpoints and training corpora are never derived from MedByte data while the account is in Non-Adaptive mode? (Procurement wants an explicit line in the attestation statement.)
- For KMS: procurement will want to see the onshore escrow process documented; can we get that as a short procedural appendix to the DPA (no secrets, just steps and parties)?

If so we can move to redlines next week. Also please send the evidence-sharing addendum template if you have one — we prefer not to sign a full NDA for diagrams.

Aaron
